depth.summary: After a string of losses, trade smaller while you find the problem, and size back up when results recover. When your account is falling, your sizing should make your trades smaller. Believing you are due a winner after losses (the gambler's fallacy) tempts you to size up when you shouldn't. The martingale system doubles the bet after every loss. Under the martingale, a few losses in a row can wipe out everything you came with. A big loss can push traders to get too aggressive trying to win it back fast.
